Checklist for parents

  • The minimum age is set by the country's law and the club's rules: check them.
  • Start only with a coach, if possible one to one.
  • A light gun, often 20 gauge, with soft cartridges; glasses and ear protection that fit.
  • Safety glasses and hearing protection from the first shot.
  • A club usually asks for written consent from parents or guardians.
  • Plan trips abroad with a child well ahead, and keep copies of all documents.
  • Documents, membership and insurance depend on the country.
  • The muzzle points in a safe direction, never at people
  • Off the stand: gun open, empty, muzzles up or down, no slings
  • On a stop command: open the gun, remove cartridges, wait
  • In lessons and training, a coach stands right next to the child on the stand
  • The same safety rules as for adults, explained before the first shot
  • Ear and eye protection in a child’s size
  • A tired child means the session is over
  • At home, guns and cartridges are locked away as the law requires
  • Ear protection for everyone near a layout, spectators and interpreters included
  • Without glasses or ear protection a shooter is treated as absent and may not shoot
  • Protection works only if it fits; plugs and muffs together protect most
  • Wash hands and face with soap after shooting and before eating
  • No food, open drinks or smoking on the stand
  • Change after shooting; wash shooting clothes apart from children’s things
  • Shoot a lot, pregnant or a child shooting: talk to a doctor
  • Ear protection, glasses and vest in children's sizes.
  • The coach teaches technique; parents support.
  • Praise effort and the routine, not the score.
  • Let the child start the talk after a round.
  • No tips from behind the stand and no comments on referee decisions.
  • The same warmth after a good round and a bad one.
  • Stand only in the spectator area, not in front of the firing line
  • Hearing protection for spectators too; glasses if you stand close
  • Quiet during shooting; applause when the shooter has finished
  • No advice during the competition and no criticism of the referee
  • Registration, competitor number on the back, squad lists and times.
  • Without hearing protection and safety glasses on the stand you are treated as absent.
  • Be ready at your turn, with cartridges for the whole round; test the gun only at the test stand.
  • Lateness costs zeros; in Compak® Sporting 25 zeros for the round.
  • No advice from the side during the round: it can cost the young shooter a yellow card.
